source: Extends prompt_bank.json's own composition_guides (rule of thirds, phi grid, diagonals, triangle, golden ratio, golden spiral, harmonic armature) with physically-grounded techniques a working photographer stacks on top of a geometry - not a second, competing taxonomy.
note: This bank holds only `techniques`. The seven named framing geometries already live in prompt_bank.json's composition_guides and are reused as-is via build_prompt.guides() - duplicating them here would give the two names to keep in sync forever. A guide (or typed custom text) is the base; techniques stack on top of either, additive and opt-in, never required. Unlike lighting's quality x source, the seven guides are already mutually exclusive by construction (one combo, one pin) and no technique here contradicts a guide or another technique - so there is no conflicts list.

negative-space.label: Negative space
negative-space.phrase: generous negative space isolating the subject
negative-space.note: Empty area as a deliberate choice, not just an unfilled frame - one of the two highest-leverage additions here, cheap and almost always applicable.

lead-room.label: Lead room
lead-room.phrase: generous lead room, the subject's gaze or motion leading toward open space in the frame
lead-room.note: The classic headroom/nose-room rule. The other highest-leverage addition - fights the single most common AI-composition tell, everything crammed dead-centre with nowhere to look into.

depth-layering.label: Depth layering
depth-layering.phrase: distinct foreground, midground, and background layers giving the shot real depth
depth-layering.note: The base composition layer already says foreground/background - this names the midground explicitly, which it never does. AI images often go flat with nothing in between.

framing-device.label: Frame within a frame
framing-device.phrase: a natural frame within the frame - a doorway, window, or archway - surrounding the subject
framing-device.note: An environmental framing device. None of the eight guides are environmental - they're all abstract grids or curves - so this is a genuinely different kind of composition, not a variation on one already there.

visual-balance.label: Visual balance
visual-balance.phrase: asymmetrical balance, weight distributed across the frame rather than centred
visual-balance.note: An explicit answer to 'does the frame feel balanced,' not implied by any guide on its own.

scale-contrast.label: Scale contrast
scale-contrast.phrase: scale contrast between subject and surroundings emphasising size
scale-contrast.note: Size read through juxtaposition against the environment, not framing geometry - matters most in a wider shot with something to compare the subject against.

pattern-repetition.label: Pattern and repetition
pattern-repetition.phrase: a repeating pattern in the environment broken by the subject
pattern-repetition.note: The subject reads as the interruption in a rhythm. The most scene-dependent of the seven - needs an environment that actually has a repeating element to break.

atmosphere.label: Atmosphere
atmosphere.phrase: a soft haze in the air separating the frame's foreground, subject, and background
atmosphere.note: Distinct from depth-layering above: that technique names the three LAYERS, this one names the air BETWEEN them. Real air isn't empty - the more of it sits between the camera and something, the lighter and softer that thing reads, which is exactly what makes distant buildings fade into a city skyline's haze.

rueckenfigur.label: Rückenfigur
rueckenfigur.phrase: a Rückenfigur - a lone figure seen from behind in the midground, gazing out over the view so the viewer looks with them
rueckenfigur.note: Caspar David Friedrich's device: the face is hidden on purpose, so the view carries the picture and the figure becomes the viewer's stand-in. Pairs with Camera's 'back shot' side, Scale contrast and Atmospheric perspective. Avoid it on a close shot or headshot, where the hidden face would be the whole frame.

atmospheric-perspective.label: Atmospheric perspective
atmospheric-perspective.phrase: atmospheric perspective, distant elements growing paler, cooler and lower in contrast as they recede into a pale haze
atmospheric-perspective.note: Distinct from `atmosphere` above: that one asks for visible haze between the layers, this one is the falloff with DISTANCE - why mountain ridges step back in fading blue layers even on a clear day. Matters most in a wide shot with real distance in it; in a small room there is not enough air for it to show.
